p.src: Meanwhile, Sun Quan led his forces against Xiakou. Huang Zu's army was defeated and his commanders slain; knowing the city could not be held, he abandoned Jiangxia and fled toward Jingzhou. Gan Ning reckoned that Huang Zu would surely flee to Jingzhou, so he stationed an ambush outside the eastern gate and waited. Huang Zu broke out through the eastern gate with several dozen horsemen. As they fled, a shout suddenly arose and Gan Ning barred their way. From horseback Huang Zu called to him, “I never treated you slightingly in former days. Why do you press me so hard now?” Gan Ning rebuked him: “When I was in Jiangxia, I rendered many distinguished services, yet you treated me as no more than a river pirate. What have you to say now?”

p.src: Huang Zu knew there was no escaping his fate and wheeled his horse to flee. Gan Ning burst through the soldiers and pursued him directly. Then shouts rose behind him, and several more riders came racing after them. Gan Ning looked and saw that it was Cheng Pu. Fearing that Cheng Pu would contend with him for the glory, Gan Ning hastily took up his bow, set an arrow to the string, and shot Huang Zu in the back. Struck by the arrow, Huang Zu tumbled from his horse. Gan Ning cut off his head, then turned back, joined forces with Cheng Pu, and returned to Sun Quan to present Huang Zu's head. Sun Quan ordered it placed in a wooden casket, intending upon his return to Jiangdong to offer it before the spirit of his late father. He richly rewarded the entire army and promoted Gan Ning to Commandant. They then discussed dividing the troops to defend Jiangxia. Zhang Zhao said, “An isolated city cannot be defended. It would be better to return to Jiangdong for the present. When Liu Biao learns that we have destroyed Huang Zu, he will surely come to avenge him. If we await his weary army with our rested forces, we shall certainly defeat him. Once Liu Biao is defeated, we may press our advantage and attack; then Jingzhou and Xiangyang can be won.” Sun Quan followed his counsel, abandoned Jiangxia, and led the army back to Jiangdong.

p.src: From inside the prison cart, Su Fei secretly sent a man to ask Gan Ning to save him. Gan Ning said, “Even if Su Fei had said nothing, could I ever forget him?” When the army reached Wujun and Kuaiji, Sun Quan ordered Su Fei beheaded so that his head might be offered together with Huang Zu's. Gan Ning entered Sun Quan's presence, knocked his head upon the floor, and pleaded through his tears: “Had Su Fei not saved me in former days, my bones would long since have filled some ditch. How could I now be serving under your command? Su Fei's crimes now merit death, but remembering the kindness he once showed me, I beg to surrender my rank and offices in redemption of his offense.” Sun Quan said, “Since he has shown you kindness, I shall pardon him for your sake. But what if he should flee?” Gan Ning replied, “Spared from execution, Su Fei will be immeasurably grateful. How could he be willing to flee? If Su Fei does flee, I am willing to present my own head beneath your steps.” Sun Quan therefore pardoned Su Fei and offered only Huang Zu's head. When the rites were over, he gave a banquet and assembled all his civil and military officers to celebrate their victory.

p.src: While they were drinking, a man at the banquet suddenly rose with a loud cry, drew his sword, and rushed straight at Gan Ning. Gan Ning hurriedly raised his chair to meet the attack. Sun Quan looked at the man in alarm and saw that it was Ling Tong. When Gan Ning had been at Jiangxia, he had shot and killed Ling Tong's father, Ling Cao; now that they had met, Ling Tong sought revenge. Sun Quan hastily restrained him, saying, “Xingba shot your father when each served a different lord; he could do no other than exert his utmost strength. Now that you belong to one house, how can you revive an old feud? In all this, defer to me.” Ling Tong knocked his head upon the floor and wept bitterly: “How can I fail to avenge a hatred that cannot exist beneath the same heaven?” Sun Quan and the assembled officers reasoned with him again and again, but Ling Tong merely glared furiously at Gan Ning. That same day Sun Quan ordered Gan Ning to take five thousand troops and one hundred warships to garrison Xiakou, thereby keeping him away from Ling Tong. Gan Ning bowed his thanks and departed with his troops for Xiakou. Sun Quan further promoted Ling Tong to Commandant Who Upholds Valor, and Ling Tong had no choice but to suppress his resentment. From that time onward, Eastern Wu built warships in great numbers and divided its troops among the defenses along the riverbanks; Sun Jing was ordered to lead a force in defense of Wujun and Kuaiji; Sun Quan personally led the main army and encamped at Chaisang; and Zhou Yu drilled the naval forces daily on Lake Poyang in readiness for war.

p.src: The tale now divides into two. Meanwhile, Xuande sent men to learn the news from Jiangdong. They returned and reported, “Eastern Wu has attacked and slain Huang Zu, and its army is now encamped at Chaisang.” Xuande invited Kongming to discuss what should be done. As they were speaking, a messenger suddenly arrived from Liu Biao, inviting Xuande to Jingzhou for consultations. Kongming said, “This must be because Jiangdong has destroyed Huang Zu. He has therefore invited you, my lord, to discuss a plan of vengeance. I shall accompany you, observe the circumstances, and act accordingly. A sound plan will present itself.” Xuande agreed. He left Yunzhang to guard Xinye and ordered Zhang Fei to accompany him to Jingzhou with five hundred men. While riding, Xuande asked Kongming, “When I meet Jingsheng, how should I answer him?” Kongming replied, “First, you should apologize for the affair at Xiangyang. If he commands you to campaign against Jiangdong, you must by no means consent. Say only that you must be allowed to return to Xinye to put your army in order.”

p.src: Following this advice, Xuande arrived in Jingzhou and took lodging at the posthouse, leaving Zhang Fei and his troops encamped outside the city. Xuande and Kongming entered the city to meet Liu Biao. When the courtesies were concluded, Xuande stood below the steps and asked forgiveness. Liu Biao said, “I already know every detail of the plot against you, worthy brother. At the time, I wished to behead Cai Mao at once and present his head to you. But everyone pleaded for him, so I spared him for the time being. I trust you will not hold it against me.” Xuande said, “General Cai had nothing to do with it. I imagine it was all the work of his subordinates.” Liu Biao said, “Now Jiangxia has fallen and Huang Zu has been slain. I therefore invited you, worthy brother, to discuss a plan of retaliation.” Xuande said, “Huang Zu was violent by nature and unable to employ worthy men; that is why this disaster befell him. If we now raise an army for a southern campaign, what shall we do should Cao Cao come from the north?” Liu Biao said, “I am now old and often ill, and can no longer manage affairs. You, worthy brother, should come and assist me. After my death, you shall become lord of Jingzhou.” Xuande said, “Why do you speak so, elder brother? How could one of Bei's poor abilities presume to assume so weighty a responsibility?”

p.src: Kongming caught Xuande's eye. Xuande said, “Allow me time to consider a sound plan.” Then he took his leave and returned to the posthouse. Kongming said, “Jingsheng wished to entrust Jingzhou to you, my lord. Why did you refuse him?” Xuande replied, “Jingsheng has treated me with kindness and every courtesy. How could I bear to take advantage of his peril and seize his domain?” Kongming sighed and said, “Truly, you are a benevolent lord!”

p.src: While they were still discussing the matter, it was suddenly announced that Liu Qi, the young lord, had come to see them. Xuande had him shown in. Liu Qi bowed through his tears and said, “My stepmother will not tolerate me, and my life may end at any moment. I beg you, uncle, to take pity and save me.” Xuande said, “This is your own family affair, worthy nephew. Why ask me about it?” Kongming smiled faintly, and Xuande asked him for a plan. Kongming said, “This is a family matter. I, Liang, dare not involve myself.” A little later, as Xuande escorted Liu Qi out, he whispered in his ear, “Tomorrow I shall have Kongming return your visit. Do thus and so, and he will surely offer you an excellent plan.” Liu Qi thanked him and departed.

p.src: The next day, Xuande feigned a stomachache and asked Kongming to return Liu Qi's visit in his stead. Kongming agreed. He rode to the young lord's residence, dismounted before the gate, and went in to see him. The young lord invited him into the rear hall. After tea, Liu Qi said, “My stepmother will not tolerate me. I pray, sir, that one word from you may save me.” Kongming said, “I, Liang, am merely a guest lodging here. How could I dare meddle in matters between another person's own flesh and blood? If any word of it leaked out, the harm would be considerable.” Having said this, he rose and took his leave. Liu Qi said, “Since you have honored me with a visit, how could I dare treat you discourteously?” He therefore detained Kongming and led him into a private chamber to drink together.

p.src: As they drank, Liu Qi again said, “My stepmother will not tolerate me. I beg you, sir, to say something that may save me.” Kongming said, “This is not a matter in which I dare offer counsel.” Having said this, he again made to take his leave. Liu Qi said, “If you will say nothing, so be it; but why must you leave at once?” Kongming then sat down once more. Liu Qi said, “I have an ancient book which I would like you to examine.” He then led Kongming up a small tower. Kongming asked, “Where is the book?” Liu Qi wept, bowed, and said, “My stepmother will not tolerate me, and my life may end at any moment. Can you truly bear to say nothing that might save me?”

p.src: Kongming rose with an angry look and was about to descend, only to find that the ladder had already been removed. Liu Qi explained, “I wish to ask you for a sound plan, but you fear that it may be divulged and therefore refuse to speak. Today we are suspended between heaven and earth; what leaves your lips will enter only my ears. Now you may surely instruct me.” Kongming said, “One who is distant cannot come between close kin. What counsel can I offer you, young master?” Liu Qi said, “Will you truly refuse to instruct me to the end? My life cannot possibly be preserved; let me die here before you.” He drew his sword and was about to cut his own throat. Kongming stopped him and said, “I have a sound plan.” Liu Qi bowed and said, “Please instruct me at once.” Kongming said, “Have you not heard the stories of Shensheng and Chong’er? Shensheng remained at home and perished, while Chong’er went abroad and survived. Now that Huang Zu has recently died, Jiangxia lacks anyone to defend it. Why do you not petition to take troops there and guard Jiangxia? In that way, you may escape disaster.”

p.src: Liu Qi bowed twice in gratitude for the counsel, then ordered his men to bring the ladder and escort Kongming down from the tower. Kongming took his leave and returned to Xuande, to whom he related the whole affair. Xuande was delighted. The next day, Liu Qi petitioned for leave to defend Jiangxia. Liu Biao hesitated, unable to decide, and asked Xuande to deliberate with him. Xuande said, “Jiangxia is a vital stronghold and certainly cannot be entrusted to just anyone. It is precisely the young master who should go there himself. You and your sons, elder brother, should take charge of affairs in the southeast; as for affairs in the northwest, I am willing to take responsibility for them.” Liu Biao said, “I recently heard that Cao Cao has constructed the Xuanwu Reservoir in Ye Commandery to train a naval force. He must intend to campaign southward, and we cannot fail to guard against him.” Xuande said, “I already know of this. Do not worry, elder brother.” He then bowed farewell and returned to Xinye. Liu Biao ordered Liu Qi to lead three thousand troops to garrison Jiangxia.

p.src: Meanwhile, Cao Cao abolished the offices of the Three Excellencies and assumed their functions himself as chancellor. He appointed Mao Jie clerk of the Eastern Bureau, Cui Yan clerk of the Western Bureau, and Sima Yi literary secretary. Sima Yi’s courtesy name was Zhongda, and he was a native of Wen County in Henei. He was the grandson of Sima Jun, former governor of Yingchuan, the son of Sima Fang, metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, and the younger brother of the registrar Sima Lang. With this, his civil administration was fully staffed, and he assembled his military commanders to discuss a southern campaign. Xiahou Dun stepped forward and said, “I have recently heard that Liu Bei is drilling his troops every day at Xinye. He is certain to become a future menace and should be dealt with promptly.”

p.src: Cao Cao at once appointed Xiahou Dun commander-in-chief, with Yu Jin, Li Dian, Xiahou Lan, and Han Hao as his deputies, and ordered him to lead one hundred thousand troops straight to Bowang, from which to threaten Xinye. Xun Yu remonstrated, “Liu Bei is a hero, and now he also has Zhuge Liang as his military adviser. The enemy must not be underestimated.” Xiahou Dun said, “Liu Bei is nothing but a rat. I shall certainly capture him.” Xu Shu said, “General, do not take Liu Xuande lightly. Now that Xuande has Zhuge Liang to assist him, he is like a tiger that has grown wings.” Cao Cao asked, “Who is Zhuge Liang?” Xu Shu replied, “Liang’s courtesy name is Kongming, and he is styled Master Sleeping Dragon. He possesses the talent to order heaven and earth and devises stratagems of unfathomable subtlety. He is truly an extraordinary man of our age and must not be slighted.”

p.src: Cao Cao asked, “How does he compare with you?” Xu Shu said, “How could I dare compare myself with Zhuge Liang? I am but the glow of a firefly, while he is the radiance of the bright moon.” Xiahou Dun said, “Yuanzhi’s words are absurd. In my eyes, Zhuge Liang is no more than a blade of grass. What is there to fear? If I do not capture Liu Bei alive and seize Zhuge Liang in a single engagement, I shall offer my own head to the chancellor.” Cao Cao said, “Send an early report of victory to set my mind at ease.” Xiahou Dun took an impassioned leave of Cao Cao and set out at the head of his army.

p.src: Now Xuande, after obtaining Kongming, treated him with the honors due a teacher. Guan Yu and Zhang Fei were displeased and said, “Kongming is young. What great learning or ability can he possess? Elder brother, you treat him with far too much honor! Nor have we yet seen any real proof of his powers!” Xuande said, “Having gained Kongming is like a fish gaining water. You two must say no more.” Hearing this, Guan Yu and Zhang Fei withdrew in silence. One day, someone delivered a yak’s tail. Xuande took it and personally began attaching it to his cap. Kongming entered, and with a grave expression said, “My lord, have you abandoned your lofty ambitions and now concern yourself only with such things?” Xuande threw the cap to the ground and apologized, saying, “I was merely using this to forget my troubles for a while.” Kongming said, “My lord, how do you judge yourself in comparison with Cao Cao?” Xuande replied, “I am his inferior.” Kongming said, “My lord’s forces number no more than a few thousand. If Cao Cao’s army should come, how will you meet it?” Xuande said, “That is precisely what troubles me, but I have yet to find a sound plan.” Kongming said, “Recruit a militia without delay. I shall train them myself, and then we will be able to await the enemy.” Xuande accordingly recruited among the people of Xinye and obtained three thousand men. Kongming drilled them in battle formations morning and evening. Suddenly a report came that Cao Cao had dispatched Xiahou Dun with one hundred thousand troops, who were advancing in a murderous rush upon Xinye. When Zhang Fei heard the news, he said to Yunzhang, “We need only send Kongming to meet the enemy.”

One day, someone delivered a yak’s tail.
Xuande took it and personally began attaching it to his cap.
Kongming entered, and with a grave expression said, “My lord, have you abandoned your lofty ambitions and now concern yourself only with such things?”
Xuande threw the cap to the ground and apologized, saying, “I was merely using this to forget my troubles for a while.”
Kongming said, “My lord, how do you judge yourself in comparison with Cao Cao?”
Xuande replied, “I am his inferior.”
Kongming said, “My lord’s forces number no more than a few thousand. If Cao Cao’s army should come, how will you meet it?”
Xuande said, “That is precisely what troubles me, but I have yet to find a sound plan.”
Kongming said, “Recruit a militia without delay. I shall train them myself, and then we will be able to await the enemy.”
Xuande accordingly recruited among the people of Xinye and obtained three thousand men.
Kongming drilled them in battle formations morning and evening.
Suddenly a report came that Cao Cao had dispatched Xiahou Dun with one hundred thousand troops, who were advancing in a murderous rush upon Xinye.
When Zhang Fei heard the news, he said to Yunzhang, “We need only send Kongming to meet the enemy.”

p.src: While they were speaking, Xuande summoned them both and said, “Xiahou Dun is leading an army against us. How shall we meet the enemy?” Zhang Fei said, “Elder brother, why not send your ‘water’?” Xuande said, “For wisdom I rely upon Kongming, but for valor I need you, my two brothers. How can you shirk your duty?” After Guan Yu and Zhang Fei had gone out, Xuande invited Kongming to discuss the situation. Kongming said, “I fear only that Guan Yu and Zhang Fei will refuse to obey my commands. If my lord wishes me to direct the army, I ask that you lend me your sword and seal of command.” Xuande immediately entrusted the sword and seal to Kongming, who then assembled all the commanders to receive their orders. Zhang Fei said to Yunzhang, “Let us go hear his orders and see how he deploys us.”

p.src: Kongming gave his orders: “To the left of Bowang stands a mountain called Mount Yu; to its right lies a wood called Anlin. Troops and horses may be hidden in ambush there. Yunzhang, take one thousand men to the front of Mount Yu and lie there in ambush. When the enemy army arrives, let it pass and do not engage. Their baggage train and provisions will certainly be in the rear. When you see fire rise in the south, lead your troops out to attack and burn their provisions. Yide, take one thousand men and hide in the valley behind Anlin. As soon as you see fire rise in the south, come out and set fire to the old supply depot at Bowang. Guan Ping and Liu Feng, take five hundred men, prepare materials for kindling fires, and wait on both sides behind Bowang Slope. When the enemy arrives at the first watch, set the fires.” He also ordered Zhao Yun recalled from Fancheng and appointed him commander of the vanguard, instructing him not to win but only to lose. “My lord shall personally lead a force in support. Each of you must act according to the plan and permit no failure.”

p.src: The two men departed. None of the generals yet knew Kongming's strategic genius; although they now obeyed his orders, they remained deeply uncertain. Kongming said to Xuande, “My lord, today you may lead the troops at once and encamp below Mount Bowang. At dusk tomorrow the enemy is certain to arrive; then, my lord, abandon the camp and withdraw. As soon as you see fire rising, turn your army back and fall upon them. I shall remain to guard the county town with Mi Zhu, Mi Fang, and five hundred soldiers, while Sun Qian and Jian Yong are to prepare a celebratory banquet and have the register of merits ready.” When all the assignments had been made, Xuande too remained uncertain.

p.src: Meanwhile, Xiahou Dun, Yu Jin, and the others led their army to Bowang. They placed half their elite troops in the vanguard, while all the rest marched escorting the supply wagons. It was autumn, and a cool west wind rose gently. As men and horses hurried onward, they suddenly saw a cloud of dust rise ahead. Dun deployed his troops and asked the local guide, “What place is this?” The guide replied, “Just ahead lies Bowang Slope, and behind it is the mouth of the Luo River valley.”

p.src: Dun ordered Yu Jin and Li Dian to hold the formation steady, then rode personally to the front of the battle line. Seeing the approaching troops from afar, Dun suddenly burst into laughter. The others asked, “Why are you laughing, General?” Dun replied, “I am laughing because Xu Yuanzhi praised Zhuge Liang before the Chancellor as a man divine. Now, judging by his deployment, he sends troops like these as his vanguard to face me. It is no different from driving dogs and sheep to fight tigers and leopards! I boasted before the Chancellor that I would capture Liu Bei and Zhuge Liang alive; today my words will surely come true.” He then spurred his horse forward. Zhao Yun rode out to meet him. Dun reviled him, saying, “You fellows follow Liu Bei like forlorn spirits trailing after a ghost!”

p.src: Enraged, Zhao Yun charged on horseback and engaged him. The two horsemen clashed, but after only a few bouts Zhao Yun feigned defeat and fled. Xiahou Dun pursued him from behind. After fleeing for some ten li, Zhao Yun wheeled his horse and fought again; after only a few more bouts, he fled once more. Han Hao urged his horse forward and warned, “Zhao Yun is luring us on; I fear there may be an ambush.” Dun said, “With an enemy like this, why should I fear even an ambush on all ten sides?” Ignoring Han Hao's warning, he pressed straight on to Bowang Slope. At the report of a cannon, Xuande himself led a force charging forward to engage them and support Zhao Yun. Xiahou Dun laughed and said to Han Hao, “So these are the troops lying in ambush! I swear I shall not halt my army until I reach Xinye tonight!” He then urged his troops onward. Xuande and Zhao Yun turned and retreated.

p.src: By then night had fallen; thick clouds covered the sky, and there was no moonlight. The wind that had risen by day blew even harder at night. Xiahou Dun thought only of driving his army onward in pursuit and slaughter. Yu Jin and Li Dian reached a narrow pass, with reeds growing thickly on both sides. Li Dian said to Yu Jin, “He who underestimates his enemy is certain to be defeated. The road south is narrow, hemmed in by mountains and streams, and crowded with trees. What shall we do if they attack with fire?” Yu Jin replied, “You are right. I shall go forward and tell the commander. You must halt the rear guard.” Li Dian reined his horse around and shouted, “Rear guard, slow your advance!” But once the men and horses had gained momentum, there was no stopping them. Yu Jin galloped ahead, shouting, “Commander of the vanguard, halt a moment!”

p.src: As Xiahou Dun was advancing, he saw Yu Jin galloping up from the rear and asked him why he had come. Yu Jin said, “The road south is narrow, hemmed in by mountains and streams, and crowded with trees. We must guard against a fire attack.” Xiahou Dun suddenly realized the danger and at once wheeled his horse around, ordering the troops to advance no farther. Before he had finished speaking, a thunderous cry arose behind them, and they saw a line of flames already blazing. Then the reeds on both sides also caught fire. In an instant, fire raged in every direction. With the wind blowing hard, the flames grew fiercer still. Cao's men and horses trampled one another, and the dead were beyond counting. Zhao Yun turned his army back and gave pursuit, while Xiahou Dun fled through smoke and flame.

p.src: Now Li Dian, seeing that the situation had turned against them, hurried back toward Bowang, only to find a force barring his way amid the firelight. The great general at their head was none other than Guan Yunchang. Li Dian spurred his horse into the melee, forced open a path, and escaped. Yu Jin saw that all the supply wagons were ablaze, so he fled along a side road. Xiahou Lan and Han Hao came to save the supplies and ran straight into Zhang Fei. They had fought only a few bouts when Zhang Fei thrust his spear and struck Xiahou Lan from his horse. Han Hao forced a path through and escaped. p.src: Meanwhile, when Kongming recalled the army, Guan Yu and Zhang Fei said to each other, “Kongming is a true hero!” They had gone only a few li when they saw Mi Zhu and Mi Fang leading troops around a small war carriage; seated solemnly within was Kongming. Guan Yu and Zhang Fei dismounted and prostrated themselves before the carriage. Before long Xuande, Zhao Yun, Liu Feng, Guan Ping, and the others all arrived. They assembled the troops, distributed the captured provisions and baggage among the officers and soldiers as rewards, and marched back to Xinye. When the people of Xinye saw the dust of their approach, they blocked the road to bow before them, saying, “That we have survived unharmed is entirely because our lord secured the service of a man of worth!”
